newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL short-term rates ease on more fund inflow.
newsitem.headline: KL short-term rates ease on more fund inflow.

text.p: Short-term interbank rates extended their fall due to the inflow of more funds, dealers said.
Some said the inflow was from overseas funds seeking higher yields due to high Malaysian interest rates.
Other dealers said the money was from the return of festival funds into the system at the tail-end of the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr celebrations.

Uncertainties surrounding the Thai baht and positive Malaysian economic data announced over the weekend also added to the liquidity due to active ringgit buying, which led to more offshore investors holding ringgit-funds.
"There's offshore money coming in because they want to take advantage of higher yields," said a Malaysian bank dealer.
Other dealers said the high-octane stockmarket was also attracting overseas money. "I do hear it's for the equity market. Futhermore, the festive money is back," said another dealers.

Trading volumes on the stockmarket have surged since last week with active play on second-tier stocks. At the midday break on Monday, total stockmarket volume stood at 524 million valued at 2.4 billion ringgit.
Dealers said one-week interbank rate was at 6.80/90 percent, down from 7.0 percent Friday. Two-week money was quoted at 7.00 from 7.10/20 and three-week at 7.00/20 against 7.20/25.
One-month rate was at 7.23/25 percent from 7.30/35 on Friday.
The three-month rate was at 7.30 from 7.30/35 and six-month to one-year were unchanged at 7.30/35.
